children: Getting dropped off at Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad by a taxi will now attract a fee, with the Adani Group-operated airport introducing a new “drop-off/visit charge” for taxis and other commercial vehicles entering the terminal area.
The airport has also raised charges for commercial vehicle “pick-ups” by 33.3 per cent, adding to the cost of using taxis to travel to and from the airport.
Taxis and other commercial four-wheelers will be charged ₹50 for drop-off/visit, with the levy going up to ₹200 if the vehicle exceeds the eight-minute limit.
The new charges also cover tempos, minibuses and buses, for which the levy can go up to ₹600 for the first 0-30 minutes, adding to the cost of airport travel for passengers using hired transport.
The new charges have been in force since October 1. Private four-wheelers are currently exempt from the new drop-off/visit charge.

The higher charges will hit passengers on their way out of the airport too. Taxis and other commercial vehicles arriving to pick up passengers will now attract a ₹200 pick-up charge, up from ₹150 earlier — a 33.3 per cent increase.
Auto-rickshaws, meanwhile, are not available for pick-up near the Terminal 1 exit, leaving passengers who want to take an auto to walk out of the terminal area to access one.
On Sunday, passengers were seen walking out of the terminal pick-up zones towards the main road with their luggage and families, apparently to avoid the increased fee.
The airport says the new charges are aimed at managing increasing traffic and supporting the upkeep, security and maintenance of its landside infrastructure.

“Airport Access Charges for commercial vehicles are an established and widely accepted practice at airports across India. Airport operators invest continuously in the development, maintenance, and security of landside infrastructure while ensuring the efficient management of increasing traffic volumes,” an SVPI spokesperson said in a statement issued here.

The spokesperson said the revised tariff is aligned with similar practices at some airports across the country and has been introduced to support the management and upkeep of landside facilities while enhancing the overall passenger experience.

The airport operator said it incurs significant expenditure on security arrangements, electricity supply, infrastructure maintenance, and personnel and facilities required for traffic management. It also provides amenities, including sanitation facilities, for drivers and visitors arriving to drop off or pick up passengers.

title: Ahmedabad airport imposes new drop-off/visit charge on taxis; raises pick-up fee by 33%
